html:
The Aq Qoyunlu, the "White Sheep" Turkomans, were a tribal confederation that ruled eastern Anatolia, Iraq and Iran from 1378 to 1503. They are shown here in 1492 and 1500, near their end.

They began around Diyarbakır as rivals of another Turkoman confederation, the Qara Qoyunlu, or "Black Sheep". Their greatest ruler, Uzun Hasan, defeated the Black Sheep in 1467 and took over their lands, beat the Timurids in 1469, and made Tabriz his capital. He sought alliances with Venice against the Ottomans, but Mehmed II defeated him at the Battle of Otlukbeli in 1473.

After Uzun Hasan's death, his heirs fought over the throne. Out of the turmoil rose the young Ismail, a grandson of Uzun Hasan through his mother. He beat the Aq Qoyunlu in 1501, took Tabriz and founded Safavid Iran. The last Aq Qoyunlu rulers were gone by 1503.
